newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain sees no inflation risk from dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain sees no inflation risk from dollar.

text.p: The Bank of Spain's governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Wednesday recent dollar strength would not push Spanish inflation higher, local news agency Europa Press reported.
"These movements in the currency market can be short-lived," Rojo told reporters who asked about the effects of the strong dollar on Spain's inflation.
"Though we can see some effect on some products with regulated prices, as is the case for fuel,...I do not think this is anything worrying for the Spanish economy," he said.
At 1130 GMT the dollar was trading at 154.06/4.11 pesetas, versus 152.63/68 late on Tuesday.
At these levels, the dollar is at the highest it has been against the peseta since January 1986.
